subject: Private GPU fleet sizing & network intake — EmpowerGrid
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@empowergrid.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial intake — on-prem GPU sizing for inference layer

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a good internal sync and the infrastructure team asked for a short written intake so they can validate networking and capacity before we scope an SOW. High-level objectives:

- Run Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) behind our border firewall in a dedicated segment.
- Target sustained inference throughput: ~12k requests/min, 95th perc latency target <= 300ms for single-turn text generation (models: MPT-30B-ish / quantized).
- Peak burst headroom up to 40k requests/min for up to 10 minutes (batching allowed).
- Model profile: mixture of short prompts (avg 75 tokens gen) and a portion of long-form (avg 600 tokens). KV-cache re-use expected for conversational flows.

Constraints to flag: limited egress bandwidth between our VPC and on-prem GPU slab (10 Gbps shared with other workloads), strict egress logging/audit requirements, and hardware procurement is on a 60–90 day timeline.

Attached is our RFP summary and a rough topology. Could you and your engineering leads review and provide:

1) A sizing sketch (GPU count by class) and networking assumptions.
2) Guidance on expected tail latency under the mix above and recommended batching/quantization knobs.
3) A short checklist of info we need to finalize procurement (NIC configs, MTU, trunking, plaintext ports, MTLS cert formats, etc.).

We'd like a concise response we can circulate to our infra and procurement. Proposed timeline: receive your initial sizing by end of day Wednesday (16 Jul), then 30-minute technical handoff on Thursday.

Thanks — happy to add Ravi from procurement once you confirm the high-level path.

-Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, EmpowerGrid
nina.patel@empowergrid.com

Attachments: empowergrid-rfp-summary.pdf, network-topology-draft.png
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@empowergrid.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial intake — on-prem GPU sizing for inference layer

Nina — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Attached is a one-page worksheet (redwood-sizing-template.xlsx) with the nominal assumptions we use to convert QPS/latency targets into GPU counts and network needs. Quick highlights up front:

- Baseline assumption: quantized 30B-class model running with half-precision KV cache and dynamic batching yields ~55 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent device under steady-state short prompts. Long-form requests reduce throughput substantially; we express as mix-weighted effective tokens/sec.
- For your stated sustained 12k reqs/min with average 75 tokens generated, that maps to ~15M tokens/min or ~250k tokens/sec. Using the per-GPU tokens/sec assumption gives an estimated 4–6 GPUs for sustained short workload.
- Accounting for the long-form tail (20% of traffic at 600 tokens), cold starts and KV fragmentation, plus a conservative 30% safety margin, recommended starting reserve: 10 GPUs (A100-80GB equivalent).
- Burst runway to 40k reqs/min: recommend either 1) pre-warmed burst pool of 6 GPUs or 2) rapid autoscale with warmed image snapshots plus a traffic shed policy. Given your 10-minute bursts and 60–90 day procurement, a warmed burst pool is safer for predictable SLAs.

Network and egress:
- 10 Gbps shared link is likely the binding constraint for your burst profile. Example calculation: with average encoded token size and request/response framing, 40k reqs/min with 75 tokens avg could approach ~6–7 Gbps outbound if responses are verbose; long-form responses push this higher. We recommend reserving a dedicated 25% of that 10 Gbps for Redwood traffic (2.5 Gbps) and negotiating a higher trunk or a dedicated link for peak windows.
- MTU: prefer 9000 for bulk KV and model sharding traffic; ensure switch NIC and TOR configs match.

Security/operational checklist (short):
- Service-to-service MTLS using customer-managed certs (we accept PEM+chain).
- Syslog forwarding for audit logs and token-level telemetry to your SIEM (TLS to collector host + mutual auth).
- NTP / time sync baseline; accurate clocks are required for tracing and log correlation.
- VLAN tagging for isolated GPU slab and an ops VLAN for management access.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Technical handoff with infra on Thu 17 Jul, 10:00–10:30 PT (we can shift if needed).
2) Provide the exact model shard sizes (if you have presets), current NIC/Switch port counts, and preferred procurement lead time.
3) If procurement wants firm pricing or a draft SOW, loop in Ben (cc'd) — he'll coordinate pricing and SOW templates.

I'll attach the sizing worksheet and a short one-page justification we use for procurement. If helpful, we can also provide a short network diagram overlay for the draft topology you sent.

Best,

Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Michael — this is very helpful, thanks. Thu 17 Jul 10:00 PT works for our infra and procurement. Ravi (procurement) is on copy; he'll want a short SOW and a list of required network ports & TLS cert formats prior to routing for PO.

Two quick clarifications:
- The 10 Gbps figure I quoted is the current trunk between the VPC edge and the on-prem slab; we can request an increase but need Redwood's concrete bandwidth asks to justify it.
- For warm pools: do you have an estimate of cost delta between keeping 6 GPUs in a warm pool vs autoscaling with 2–3 minute spin-up? Procurement will want unit math.

I'll attach our procurement contact sheet in a follow-up; we can also provide a more detailed request form if that helps.

Thanks — see you Thursday.

-Nina

Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial intake — on-prem GPU sizing for inference layer

Great — quick prep notes for the technical handoff tomorrow:

1) Bandwidth ask: for the worst-case burst sizing (40k req/min with 75 avg tokens) we recommend planning for 10 Gbps steady for application traffic plus headroom for KV sync and shard rebalance. Practically that means requesting a temporary trunk increase to 25 Gbps during acceptance testing or provisioning a dedicated 25 Gbps cross-connect for production. We'll provide the packet-level estimate (MB/s per request) during the call so you can paste it into your ticket.

2) Warm-pool cost delta: Ben — can you drop two numbers (monthly cost per A100-80GB warm-reserved vs on-demand spin-up) into the call?

3) Deliverables we'll provide within 48 hours after the call: a) a 1-page network checklist (NIC, MTU, VLAN, ports), b) a proposed SOW draft, and c) a short runbook for warm-pool operation and failover.

Action items:
- Nina / EmpowerGrid: confirm whether you can provision a 25 Gbps test trunk for our acceptance window.
- Procurement (Ravi): send preferred SOW template or PO cadence.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare cost delta table and draft SOW skeleton.

Look forward to the handoff.

Best,

Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
